Seminar Title:

Design of Soft Sensors Based on Electrochemical Features: Application in Specialty and Commodity Chemical Production Processes

Seminar Type:

Defence Seminar

Department:

Chemical Engineering

Speaker Name:

Ashutosh Kumar Pathak ( Rollno : 521ch6009)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

New Seminar Hall (CH)

Date and Time:

31 Jul 2026 11 am

Contact:

Madhusree Kundu

Abstract:

Conventional monitoring of commodity and specialty chemicals manufacturing processes relies on analytical instruments like HPLC, GC-MS, and FT-IR, which, though accurate, are costly, time-intensive, and require skilled operators. This study explores electrochemical soft sensor-based quantification for esterification, transesterification, and fermentation, aiming to reduce instrumentation burdens while enabling adaptive monitoring. Esterification of butyric acid with n-butanol and acetic acid with butanol was studied using concentration-based and activity (UNIFAC) kinetic models. Conversion of butyric acid was mapped through electrochemical techniques (CV and EIS), with regression models (MLR, PLS) developed as soft sensors to estimate acid conversion. An impedimetric database supported a multifunction MLR model predicting both concentration and reaction rate, while a Takagi&ndashSugeno fuzzy inference system estimated acetic acid concentration. For biodiesel, waste cooking oil was trans-esterified with methanol. Yield was correlated with EIS parameters and modeled using ANNs (FNN, RBF, GRNN), with FNN outperforming others and serving as a surrogate in reinforcement learning (RL) optimization of the process. Finally, simulated fermentation of glucose with Clostridium tyrobutyricum was analyzed via EIS. Impedance parameters enabled the development of an Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) to predict acetic and butyric acid concentrations. Overall, this work demonstrates the potential of electrochemical data integrated with regression, fuzzy logic, ANN, and hybrid ANFIS models to advance intelligent monitoring and control in chemical and biochemical processes.
